We first subclustered the Schwann cell group (16,259 cells) and identified 15 clusters all of which expressed pan-Schwann cell markers (S100b and Sox10), except for cluster 9 (746 cells) which comprised putative doublets (Fig. 2a and Supplementary Fig. 5).

Based on known markers, we were able to further classify each cluster into one of the following subtypes: myelinating Schwann cells (Prx), non-myelinating Remak Schwann cells (Gfap), dividing Schwann cells (Mki67), repair cells (Ngfr, also known as p75NTR), as well as a cluster of cells we termed transition cells (Fig. 2b, c and Supplementary Fig. 5).
